title: React.memo
description:
## React.memo When a parent re-renders, **all** of its children re-render by default — even if their props are identical to last time. `React.memo` wraps a component so React skips the render when the props shallow-compare equal. ```jsx const Child = React.memo(function Child({ name }) { return

Hello, {name}

; }); ``` Now `` only re-runs when `name` changes — re-renders of the parent don't propagate. > Like `useMemo`, this is a tool for measured problems. Don't blanket-wrap everything. ### Your Task Build a parent counter and a memoized greeting child: 1. Define a memoized component `Greeting` that renders `

Hello, {name}!

` 2. In `App`, hold a `count` state 3. Render `` and a `

Count: {count}

` 4. Button `#bump` increments count by 1
